kinda
of made a post about this, my goal is still the same, altough it seems impossibile to fix this issue, (For context, I want my game to be in basic rpg maker fullscreen, with the chunky borders, the one that is set when you press f4, but doing that blurs  pixels, and adding pixel perfect plugins works, but make the pixels laggy as shown in the pictures of that previous post) i sometimes bump into very close solutions, this time with the
Game Upgrade Plugin
, i realized i can get it to work by putting the game resolution the one i want, that can make it exactly like i want it, with pixel perfect scaling and no laggy pixels when moving, the issue is this changes the camera size, and it needs to be too big to meet the requirements, one workaround would be to make everything bigger, but i'm already far into the project and besides it would be extremely messy to have such big sprites, could there be any other workaround for this?
In case there is none, i would also be open to not-too invading filters, i've tried crt ones and those kinda of hide the issue but don't really fit the vibe, thanks to everyone
Edit: Another "clue" is that this laggy pixels  thing when moving only happens when the game is in f4 fullscreen, while it's perfcetly fine when it's windowed

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
unfortunately you cannot simply rewrite the physical laws of the universe...
There are correlations that cannot be ignored, and all tries to work around them will cause other problems.
For example a pixel is the base unit of 2D pictures that cannot be divided, and the resolution is (in case of MV/MZ) 48 pixel per tile (too many people confuse the screen size to be a resolution, but that is simply wrong.
I don't have time to explain everything, so I link you to a few posts in the last days where I had time to explain things:
